meanings: to coerce (sb into doing sth bad)

components.note: 弓 (bow) — the weapon being drawn.
丨 depicts the taut drawstring being pulled back — giving 引 its meaning 'to pull, draw out, attract.'
讠 (speech) on the left shows this involves words.
秀 (elegant, refined) on the right suggests alluring words, giving 诱 its meaning 'to entice, to lure.'

example.hanzi: 毒品贩子想引诱那个孩子上钩。
example.pinyin: Dúpǐn fànzi xiǎng yǐnyòu nàge háizi shàng gōu.
example.english: The drug dealer wanted to lure that child into a trap.
example.fact: The Venus flytrap lures insects with a sweet-smelling nectar secreted along the rim of its hinged leaves; once an insect brushes two trigger hairs within about 20 seconds of each other, the trap snaps shut in under a tenth of a second — one of the fastest movements in the plant kingdom.

components.note: 山 is a simple picture of three mountain peaks in a row.
羊 is a simple picture of a sheep's head, seen from the front, with two curved horns at the top.

example.hanzi: 那只山羊爬到了陡峭的岩石上。
example.pinyin: Nà zhī shānyáng pá dào le dǒuqiào de yánshí shàng.
example.english: That goat climbed onto the steep rocks.
example.fact: Mountain goats have cloven hooves with an inner pad that acts like a suction cup, letting them grip near-vertical rock faces and cross cliffs over 1,000 feet tall. Wild goats were among the first animals domesticated by humans, around 10,000 years ago in the Zagros Mountains of present-day Iran.

meanings: to see with one's own eyes

components.note: 目 depicts an eye turned on its side, with the outline and pupil visible — later straightened into today's rectangular shape.
目 (eye) — 睹 is an action done with the eyes.
者 (zhě) gives a sound distantly related to dǔ, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 许多市民目睹了那场车祸的发生。
example.pinyin: Xǔduō shìmín mùdǔ le nà chǎng chēhuò de fāshēng.
example.english: Many residents witnessed that car accident happen.
example.fact: Eyewitness memory is far less reliable than most people assume — the Innocence Project has found that mistaken eyewitness identification played a role in more than 60% of the wrongful convictions later overturned by DNA evidence in the United States.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 潜 describes hiding beneath the surface of water.
替 (tì) gives a sound distantly related to qián, having drifted apart over time.
土 (earth/soil) — 在 originally related to standing on the ground
才 (cái) gives the sound — 在 is pronounced zài, a close match

example.hanzi: 科学家正在研究这种药物的潜在副作用。
example.pinyin: Kēxuéjiā zhèngzài yánjiū zhè zhǒng yàowù de qiánzài fùzuòyòng.
example.english: Scientists are researching the potential side effects of this drug.
example.fact: Penicillin was discovered in 1928 when Alexander Fleming noticed that mold accidentally contaminating a petri dish was killing the bacteria around it. He almost threw the dish away, not immediately recognizing its potential — it would go on to save an estimated 200 million lives.

components.note: 心 (heart) — 恶 relates to an evil or malicious state of heart/mind
亚 (yà) gives a sound distantly related to 恶's reading è, having drifted apart over time
化 depicts a standing person (亻) next to an inverted person (匕, a person turned upside down) — the image of one form changing into another, giving 化 its meaning 'to change, to transform.'

example.hanzi: 病人的病情在夜里突然恶化了。
example.pinyin: Bìngrén de bìngqíng zài yèlǐ tūrán èhuà le.
example.english: The patient's condition suddenly worsened during the night.
example.fact: The Aral Sea, once the world's fourth-largest lake, has shrunk to about 10% of its original volume since the 1960s after Soviet irrigation projects diverted its feeder rivers, a decline environmental scientists often cite as one of the fastest man-made ecological disasters on record.

components.note: 纟 (thread) — 终 originally referred to the end of a woven thread, extended to mean 'end, final'
冬 (dōng) gives a loose sound connection to 终's reading zhōng
木 (wood) — 极 originally named the ridgepole, the highest beam of a roof, extended to 'extreme, utmost.'
及 (jí) gives the sound — 极 is also pronounced jí, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 这场比赛被称为两位棋手的终极对决。
example.pinyin: Zhè chǎng bǐsài bèi chēng wéi liǎng wèi qíshǒu de zhōngjí duìjué.
example.english: This match was called the ultimate showdown between the two chess players.
example.fact: Physicists sometimes describe the search for a single theory unifying gravity with quantum mechanics as the field's 'ultimate' goal. Albert Einstein spent the last three decades of his life chasing such a unified field theory and never succeeded — the problem remains unsolved today.

components.note: 另 (other, separate) — 别 relates to distinguishing one thing from another.
刂 (knife) — cutting things apart to sort them gave 别 its meaning 'to separate' or 'other,' and later, 'don't' as a command.
夂 (a foot, to go) — 处 relates to arriving somewhere.
卜 (a mark or flag) — planting a marker after arriving gave 处 its meaning of 'a place' or 'to settle, deal with.'

example.hanzi: 这里没有空房间了,你得去别处看看。
example.pinyin: Zhèlǐ méiyǒu kōng fángjiān le, nǐ děi qù biéchù kànkan.
example.english: There are no empty rooms here, you'll have to look elsewhere.
example.fact: Monarch butterflies that hatch in the United States and Canada each fall migrate up to 3,000 miles to a few specific fir-forested mountains in central Mexico, a journey no single butterfly completes twice — the return trip north is finished by their offspring instead.

components.note: Depicts a young wheat or tree branch that has not yet borne fruit — the image of something still incomplete, the source of 未's meaning 'not yet.'
口 (mouth) — 知 relates to speaking what one knows.
矢 (shǐ) gives a hint of the sound — 知 is pronounced zhī, a connection that has faded over time.

example.hanzi: 地图上标出了一片未知的区域。
example.pinyin: Dìtú shàng biāo chū le yī piàn wèizhī de qūyù.
example.english: The map marked out an area of unknown territory.
example.fact: More than 80% of the world's oceans remain unmapped, unobserved, and unexplored by humans, according to NOAA. We have better maps of the surface of Mars and the Moon than we do of the ocean floor beneath our own planet's waters.

components.note: 求 originally depicted a fur coat, drawn with tufts of fur along the edges; the sense 'to seek, to request' developed later, possibly because a warm coat was something people sought out, and the original meaning was eventually replaced by 裘.
攵 (a hand taking action) — 救 describes the act of rescuing someone.
求 (qiú) gives a sound close to jiù, sharing a similar rhyme.

example.hanzi: 船员发出信号求救。
example.pinyin: Chuányuán fāchū xìnhào qiújiù.
example.english: The crew sent out a signal to seek help.
example.fact: The distress call 'SOS' was adopted internationally in 1906 not because it stands for any phrase, but because its Morse code pattern — three dots, three dashes, three dots — is simple and unmistakable to transmit and recognize under pressure, even for an untrained operator.

components.note: 走 (run/walk) — relates to 越's meaning 'to exceed, cross over,' running past a boundary.
戉 (yuè) gives the sound — 越 is also pronounced yuè, an exact match.
犭 (dog) on the left represents a guard dog.
讠 (speech) suggests an accusation or a legal case being spoken.
犬 (dog) on the right completes the scene, giving 狱 its meaning 'prison, lawsuit.'

example.hanzi: 那名囚犯计划从监狱越狱。
example.pinyin: Nà míng qiúfàn jìhuà cóng jiānyù yuèyù.
example.english: That prisoner planned to break out of the prison.
example.fact: Alcatraz Federal Penitentiary in San Francisco Bay was long marketed as escape-proof, yet in 1962 three inmates carved through cell walls with spoons, built dummy heads from soap and hair to fool guards, and vanished on a makeshift raft; their fate was never conclusively determined.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 讲 relates to speaking, explaining, telling
井 (jǐng) gives a sound close to 讲's reading jiǎng
辶 (to walk) — narrating something is like walking a listener through events
术 (shù) gives the sound — an exact match with 述's reading shù

example.hanzi: 这本小说讲述了一个渔村的故事。
example.pinyin: Zhè běn xiǎoshuō jiǎngshù le yī gè yúcūn de gùshi.
example.english: This novel tells the story of a fishing village.
example.fact: Homer's Odyssey, one of the oldest surviving works of Western literature at roughly 2,800 years old, was composed and transmitted orally for generations before it was ever written down, relying on rhythmic verse patterns that helped bards memorize thousands of lines.

components.note: 夕 (evening/night), doubled — two nights stacked together suggested the idea of accumulation, giving 多 its meaning of 'many, much.'
攵 (a hand with a stick, action) — 数 relates to the action of counting.
娄 (lóu) gives a hint of the sound — 数 is pronounced shù, a connection that has drifted over time.

example.hanzi: 多数与会者都同意这个方案。
example.pinyin: Duōshù yùhuìzhě dōu tóngyì zhège fāng'àn.
example.english: The majority of attendees agreed with this proposal.
example.fact: In many parliamentary democracies, a 'supermajority' of two-thirds is required to amend a constitution — the same two-thirds threshold the US Congress needs to override a presidential veto, a deliberately high bar designed to force broad consensus before fundamental rules can change.

components.note: 直 (straight, upright) — 真 relates to something level and true.
几 (a small table) — an object placed level and true on a table gave 真 its meaning 'real' or 'true.'
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.

example.hanzi: 这个动画角色后来被真人演员搬上了银幕。
example.pinyin: Zhège dònghuà juésè hòulái bèi zhēnrén yǎnyuán bān shàng le yínmù.
example.english: This animated character was later brought to the screen by a real-life actor.
example.fact: The 2019 live-action remake of The Lion King used no traditional cameras at all — every scene was generated inside a virtual-reality game engine, with filmmakers wearing VR headsets to 'walk' through a photorealistic digital savanna and frame shots as if filming real animals.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh/body) — part of the body.
匈 here representing an enclosed cavity, together giving 胸 its meaning 'chest, breast.'
口 is a simple picture of an open mouth.

example.hanzi: 他跑完步后感觉胸口发闷。
example.pinyin: Tā pǎo wán bù hòu gǎnjué xiōngkǒu fā mèn.
example.english: He felt tightness in his chest after finishing his run.
example.fact: The human heart sits slightly left of center in the chest and beats roughly 100,000 times a day, pumping about 2,000 gallons of blood — enough to fill a small backyard swimming pool — through nearly 60,000 miles of blood vessels.

components.note: 人 (person) forms the top of the character.
八, shown here as a dividing line, suggests separation or a boundary — together with 人 above, giving 介 its meaning 'to lie between, to introduce.'
入 depicts a simple wedge or arrow shape pointing inward, showing the direction of entering.

example.hanzi: 警方及时介入,阻止了冲突升级。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng jíshí jièrù, zǔzhǐ le chōngtū shēngjí.
example.english: The police intervened in time, preventing the conflict from escalating.
example.fact: The 1962 Cuban Missile Crisis brought the US and Soviet Union to the brink of nuclear war; declassified records later revealed that a single Soviet submarine officer, Vasili Arkhipov, refused to authorize a nuclear torpedo launch during a tense standoff, a decision historians credit with averting catastrophe.

components.note: 车 (cart) — 软 originally described a cart with cushioned, springy wheels, giving a soft ride.
欠 (qiàn) gives a sound distantly related to ruǎn, having drifted apart over time.
亻 (person) — 件 relates to a person separating something into parts.
牛 (ox) — dividing an ox into pieces gave 件 its meaning of an individual 'item' or 'piece,' now used as a measure word for objects and matters.

example.hanzi: 这家公司开发了一款很受欢迎的软件。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī kāifā le yī kuǎn hěn shòu huānyíng de ruǎnjiàn.
example.english: This company developed a very popular piece of software.
example.fact: The term 'software' was first used in print in 1958 by statistician John Tukey, who coined it to distinguish programs from the physical 'hardware' of a computer — a distinction that didn't fully catch on in common usage until the personal computer boom of the late 1970s and 1980s.

components.note: 礻 (spirit/altar) — 福 relates to blessings granted by the spirits
畐 (fú) gives the sound — an exact match with 福's reading fú
牛 (ox) — 特 originally referred to a male ox singled out for sacrifice, a special animal set apart from the herd.
寺 (sì) gives a hint of the sound — 特 is pronounced tè, a connection that has drifted over time.

example.hanzi: 福特汽车公司成立于1903年。
example.pinyin: Fútè qìchē gōngsī chénglì yú 1903 nián.
example.english: Ford Motor Company was founded in 1903.
example.fact: Henry Ford didn't invent the automobile or the assembly line, but by adapting moving assembly-line techniques to car manufacturing in 1913, he cut the time to build a Model T from about 12 hours to roughly 90 minutes, making cars affordable to ordinary workers for the first time.

components.note: 屮 (a young sprout) growing up and out of 凵 (a container or pit) — a picture of something emerging, hence 'going out.'
A picture of a nose; because people in ancient China would point to their own nose when referring to themselves, the character came to mean 'self.'

example.hanzi: 这句名言出自一位古代哲学家。
example.pinyin: Zhè jù míngyán chūzì yī wèi gǔdài zhéxuéjiā.
example.english: This famous quote comes from an ancient philosopher.
example.fact: The phrase 'survival of the fittest' is often attributed to Charles Darwin, but he never coined it himself — it actually comes from philosopher Herbert Spencer, who used it in 1864 to summarize Darwin's theory of natural selection, and Darwin only adopted the phrase in later editions of On the Origin of Species.

components.note: 平 depicts a balance scale drawn level and symmetrical — a simple picture of flatness and equality.
⺮ (bamboo) — 等 pictures bamboo strips, once used as writing tablets, being sorted.
寺 (originally a government office, later 'temple') — sorting and arranging bamboo documents at an official court gave 等 its meanings 'to wait,' 'rank,' and 'etc.'

example.hanzi: 宪法规定所有公民在法律面前平等。
example.pinyin: Xiànfǎ guīdìng suǒyǒu gōngmín zài fǎlǜ miànqián píngděng.
example.english: The constitution stipulates that all citizens are equal before the law.
example.fact: New Zealand became the first self-governing country to grant women the right to vote nationally, in 1893 — nearly three decades before the United States did so in 1920 and more than fifty years before France, which did not grant women suffrage until 1944.

components.note: 彳 depicts a step with the left foot; together with 亍 (a step with the right foot), 行 shows a person walking or moving.
亍 depicts a step with the right foot, complementing 彳 to form the idea of walking or travel.
The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'
辶 (to walk, movement) — 通 relates to passing through or getting somewhere.
甬 (yǒng) gives a hint of the sound — 通 is pronounced tōng, a connection that has shifted over time.

example.hanzi: 这个计划在实际操作中行不通。
example.pinyin: Zhège jìhuà zài shíjì cāozuò zhōng xíngbutōng.
example.english: This plan won't work in actual practice.
example.fact: Prohibition in the United States, which banned the sale of alcohol from 1920 to 1933, is widely cited by economists and historians as a policy that simply didn't work — it fueled a massive black market, empowered organized crime syndicates, and was ultimately repealed after 13 years.

components.note: 阝 (a mound/city) — represents a place being traveled to.
迶 depicts walking or moving along a path — following someone to the city gave 随 its meaning 'to follow, along with.'

The oracle-bone form shows a foot (夊) trailing behind, an image of lagging or coming afterward, which gave 后 its meaning 'behind, after' — a sense later merged with an unrelated character meaning 'queen, empress.'

example.hanzi: 他先做了自我介绍,随后开始了演讲。
example.pinyin: Tā xiān zuò le zìwǒ jièshào, suíhòu kāishǐ le yǎnjiǎng.
example.english: He first introduced himself, and then began his speech.
example.fact: Total solar eclipses often trigger a rapid sequence of atmospheric changes: temperatures can drop by 10 degrees Fahrenheit or more within minutes of totality, and afterward, as the sun re-emerges, winds and temperatures snap back close to normal within about half an hour.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 滑 describes something as slick or slippery, like a wet surface.
骨 (gǔ) is only distantly related in sound to huá — the connection has drifted apart to the point of being barely recognizable.
雨 (rain) — 雪 belongs to the group of weather words built on 雨, since snow falls the way rain does.
彐 gives a sound distantly related to xuě, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 他们每年冬天都去阿尔卑斯山滑雪。
example.pinyin: Tāmen měinián dōngtiān dōu qù Ā'ěrbēisī Shān huáxuě.
example.english: They go skiing in the Alps every winter.
example.fact: Skiing may be far older than commonly assumed — a rock carving in Norway dated to around 5,000 years ago depicts a person on skis, and wooden ski fragments preserved in Russian peat bogs have been carbon-dated to roughly 6,000 years old.

components.note: 八 (a hand shape) — one of two hands shown reaching toward the same object.
廾 (two hands together) — jointly holding up one object, giving 共 its meaning 'together, joint, common.'
口 (mouth) — ties to harmony as speaking together in accord
禾 (hé, grain) gives the sound — matches 和's pronunciation hé
兄 (elder brother, i.e. companion) — 党's meaning 'party, group, faction' relates to people bonded like brothers.
尚 (shàng) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from dǎng.

example.hanzi: 共和党在那次选举中赢得了多数席位。
example.pinyin: Gònghédǎng zài nà cì xuǎnjǔ zhōng yíngdé le duōshù xíwèi.
example.english: The Republican Party won a majority of seats in that election.
example.fact: The Republican Party's mascot, the elephant, was popularized by political cartoonist Thomas Nast in an 1874 Harper's Weekly illustration; Nast also independently popularized the donkey as the Democratic Party's symbol, and both images have stuck in American politics for a century and a half.

components.note: 雨 (rain) — 零 originally described light, scattered rain, extended to mean a fragment or zero.
令 (lìng) is an exact match for the sound of 零, differing only in tone.
亻 (person) — 件 relates to a person separating something into parts.
牛 (ox) — dividing an ox into pieces gave 件 its meaning of an individual 'item' or 'piece,' now used as a measure word for objects and matters.

example.hanzi: 这台机器缺少了一个重要零件。
example.pinyin: Zhè tái jīqì quēshǎo le yī gè zhòngyào língjiàn.
example.english: This machine is missing an important part.
example.fact: A modern jet engine like the GE9X, used on the Boeing 777X, contains over 30,000 individual parts, and airlines track many of them by unique serial number for their entire operational life so mechanics can trace the exact history of any single component.

components.note: 夕 (evening/night), doubled — two nights stacked together suggested the idea of accumulation, giving 多 its meaning of 'many, much.'
人 (person) sits atop the character, loosely suggesting shelter for a person.
The character originally depicted a simple hut or shelter with extra room to spare, a sense that extended over time to mean 'surplus, remaining.'

example.hanzi: 他觉得自己的解释显得多余。
example.pinyin: Tā juéde zìjǐ de jiěshì xiǎnde duōyú.
example.english: He felt that his explanation seemed unnecessary.
example.fact: The human appendix was long dismissed by biologists as a useless evolutionary leftover, but research published in the 2000s suggests it may act as a safe house for beneficial gut bacteria, helping repopulate the intestines after illnesses like cholera or dysentery wipe them out.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 援 describes reaching out to help someone by hand.
爰 depicts one hand passing something to another, reinforcing the idea of lending aid — together giving 援 its meaning 'to help, to aid.'
力 (strength) — 助 relates to helping, lending one's strength
且 (qiě) gives a loose sound connection to 助's reading zhù

example.hanzi: 国际社会向灾区提供了大量援助。
example.pinyin: Guójì shèhuì xiàng zāiqū tígōng le dàliàng yuánzhù.
example.english: The international community provided substantial aid to the disaster area.
example.fact: The Marshall Plan, launched by the United States in 1948, provided over $13 billion (roughly $150 billion in today's dollars) to help rebuild sixteen war-torn Western European countries after World War II, and is widely credited with helping the region avoid economic collapse and the spread of famine.

meanings: sb who takes an exam for sb else

components.note: 木 (wood) — early spears and rifle stocks were made of wood.
仓 (cāng) gives a sound close to qiāng, sharing the same rhyme.
手 is a simple picture of an open hand with the fingers spread out.

example.hanzi: 警方正在追捕那名逃跑的枪手。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng zhèngzài zhuībǔ nà míng táopǎo de qiāngshǒu.
example.english: The police are pursuing the gunman who fled.
example.fact: Annie Oakley, one of history's most celebrated sharpshooters, could reportedly split a playing card edge-on from 30 paces and hit a dime tossed into the air; she toured with Buffalo Bill's Wild West show for 17 years, astonishing audiences across the US and Europe in the late 1800s.

components.note: 生 (to grow, life) sits atop the character, tying 青 to the fresh, vivid color of new plant growth.

丹 (a mineral pigment, cinnabar red) contributes the sense of a vivid dye or pigment; together the two elements gave 青 its meaning of a blue-green color, later broadened to include youth and freshness.
日 (sun) — 春 relates to spring's longer, sunnier days.

example.hanzi: 这部电影讲述了几个年轻人的青春故事。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng jiǎngshù le jǐ gè niánqīngrén de qīngchūn gùshi.
example.english: This movie tells the story of several young people's youth.
example.fact: Axolotls, a type of salamander native to Mexico, can regenerate entire lost limbs, portions of their spinal cord, and even parts of their heart and brain throughout their lives — an extraordinary form of biological youthfulness that has made them a major focus of regenerative medicine research.

components.note: 犭 (dog) — an old link behind 独's meaning 'alone, single, solitary'
虫 (chóng) gives a loose sound connection to 独's reading dú
夂 (a foot, to go) — 处 relates to arriving somewhere.
卜 (a mark or flag) — planting a marker after arriving gave 处 its meaning of 'a place' or 'to settle, deal with.'

example.hanzi: 她喜欢周末一个人在家独处。
example.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan zhōumò yī gè rén zàijiā dúchǔ.
example.english: She likes being alone at home by herself on weekends.
example.fact: Christopher Knight lived alone in the Maine woods for 27 years without a single conversation with another person, surviving through quiet, careful burglary of nearby cabins for food and supplies, until he was finally caught in 2013 — one of the most extreme documented cases of long-term solitude.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — relates directly to 持's meaning 'to hold, maintain.'
寺 (sì) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from chí.
月 (yuè) here actually derives from 肉 (meat) — 有 originally depicted a hand holding meat, meaning 'to possess'; it also lends a loose phonetic connection to yǒu.

example.hanzi: 他持有这家公司百分之十的股份。
example.pinyin: Tā chíyǒu zhè jiā gōngsī bǎi fēn zhī shí de gǔfèn.
example.english: He holds ten percent of the shares in this company.
example.fact: The Louvre Museum's most famous painting, the Mona Lisa, has been owned by the French state since the 16th century and is legally inalienable — a special law makes it, and other pieces in French national collections, permanently prohibited from being sold or given away.

components.note: Originally a pictograph of a musical bell or instrument hung in a frame; this shape was later reused to write the unrelated directional word 南, 'south.'
Represents the round shape of a melon hanging on the vine.

example.hanzi: 每年秋天他们都会做南瓜派。
example.pinyin: Měinián qiūtiān tāmen dōu huì zuò nánguā pài.
example.english: Every autumn they make pumpkin pie.
example.fact: The largest pumpkin ever officially weighed, grown in Minnesota in 2023, tipped the scales at over 2,700 pounds — roughly the weight of a small car — and giant-pumpkin growers achieve such sizes partly by removing all but one fruit per vine so it receives the plant's entire energy supply.

components.note: 力 (strength) — 勋 relates to achievement earned through effort.
员 (yuán) gives a sound only distantly related to xūn today, having drifted apart over time.
音 (sound/music) — represents a musical piece.
十 (ten) — ten musical movements or sections making up a complete piece gave 章 its meaning 'chapter, section, composition.'

example.hanzi: 这位老兵胸前挂着好几枚勋章。
example.pinyin: Zhè wèi lǎobīng xiōngqián guà zhe hǎojǐ méi xūnzhāng.
example.english: This veteran had several medals hanging on his chest.
example.fact: The Medal of Honor, the United States' highest military decoration, has been awarded fewer than 3,600 times since its creation in 1861; each medal is individually cast, and by law it can never be bought or sold, only issued directly by the government.

components.note: 人 (people) over 云 (clouds/say) — a picture of people gathering and speaking together, related to 会's meanings 'to meet' and 'to know how to.'
讠 (speech) — 计 relates to counting or planning through words and numbers.
十 (shí) gives a hint of the sound — 计 is pronounced jì, a connection that has shifted significantly over time.

example.hanzi: 她大学毕业后成为了一名会计。
example.pinyin: Tā dàxué bìyè hòu chéngwéi le yī míng kuàijì.
example.english: After graduating from university, she became an accountant.
example.fact: Double-entry bookkeeping, the accounting method still used worldwide today, was first systematically described in 1494 by Italian friar Luca Pacioli, sometimes called the 'father of accounting,' in a mathematics textbook that also happened to include the first published rules of the game we now know as blackjack.

components.note: 木 (tree) — 相 pictures looking closely at a tree.
目 (eye) — staring closely at a tree to examine it gave 相 the meaning 'to observe' or, later, 'each other, mutual.'
A pictograph of half of a split tree trunk, shown in cross-section (compare 爿, the other half) — the source of 片's meaning 'a thin slice, piece.'

example.hanzi: 墙上挂着一张全家的相片。
example.pinyin: Qiáng shàng guà zhe yī zhāng quánjiā de xiàngpiàn.
example.english: A photograph of the whole family hangs on the wall.
example.fact: The oldest surviving photograph of a person, taken by Louis Daguerre around 1838 on a Paris street, shows a man having his shoes shined; he appears only because he stood still long enough during the several-minute exposure, while everyone else walking by moved too fast to be captured.

components.note: 莫 originally depicted the sun (日) sinking into a thicket of grass (艹, doubled), a picture of dusk; the sense was later borrowed to write the unrelated negative word 'not, none,' and a new character, 暮, was created to carry the original meaning of 'evening.'
斤 (an axe) originally tied 斯 to the act of splitting or chopping wood.
其 (qí) is close in sound to 斯's reading sī, and in modern usage the character mainly serves as a phonetic transcription element in foreign names and place names, such as 莫斯科 (Moscow).
禾 (grain, a rice/wheat plant) — 科 relates to sorting and measuring crops.
斗 (a measuring ladle) — measuring grain into ordered categories gave 科 its meaning 'a branch of study' or 'a department.'

example.hanzi: 莫斯科是俄罗斯的首都。
example.pinyin: Mòsīkē shì Éluósī de shǒudū.
example.english: Moscow is the capital of Russia.
example.fact: The Moscow Metro, opened in 1935, is famous for stations built like underground palaces, with marble columns, mosaics, and chandeliers; Mayakovskaya station is decorated with 34 ceiling mosaics depicting the sky at different times of day, designed partly to double as an air-raid shelter during World War II.

meanings: to ride (in a train or other vehicle)

components.note: 北 here representing two feet or footprints, one behind the other.
禾 (a stalk of grain), here standing in for a tree or ladder — together depicting someone climbing up, giving 乘 its meaning 'to ride, to get onto.'
从 (two people, one following another) — depicts people together.
土 (earth/ground) — two people seated on the ground gave 坐 its meaning 'to sit.'

example.hanzi: 我们乘坐火车去了上海。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen chéngzuò huǒchē qù le Shànghǎi.
example.english: We took a train to Shanghai.
example.fact: The Shanghai Maglev Train, which uses magnetic levitation to float above its track without touching it, can reach speeds of up to 268 miles per hour, making the roughly 19-mile trip from downtown Shanghai to Pudong International Airport in under eight minutes.

components.note: 发 is the simplified form of 發, which originally combined a bow (弓) with a symbol for feet moving apart, depicting an arrow shooting outward — the source of 发's meaning 'to issue, to send out, to develop.'
Hand — shaking is often done with the hands.
Gives the sound dǒu, matching the character's reading.

example.hanzi: 她冷得浑身发抖。
example.pinyin: Tā lěng de húnshēn fādǒu.
example.english: She was shivering all over from the cold.
example.fact: Shivering is the body's way of generating heat through rapid, involuntary muscle contractions, and it can boost metabolic heat production by up to five times the resting rate — though it's so energy-intensive that prolonged shivering can exhaust a person's glycogen reserves within about 15 to 20 minutes.

components.note: The ancient form of 监 depicts a person bending over a basin of water to look at their own reflection, since bronze mirrors did not yet exist — the act of closely watching one's own image gave 监 its meaning 'to observe, to supervise.'
目 (eye) — supervising, 督's meaning, involves watching closely.
叔 (shū) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading dū has diverged.

example.hanzi: 工程建设过程需要专人监督。
example.pinyin: Gōngchéng jiànshè guòchéng xūyào zhuānrén jiāndū.
example.english: The construction process needs to be supervised by a dedicated person.
example.fact: The International Atomic Energy Agency, founded in 1957, sends inspectors to nuclear facilities in over 180 countries to monitor and verify that nuclear materials are not being diverted toward weapons programs, using tools ranging from surveillance cameras to tamper-proof seals on equipment.

components.note: 阝 (mound/hill) — 阻 originally described a hill or ridge blocking one's path.
且 (qiě) gives a sound distantly related to zǔ, having drifted apart over time.
石 (stone) — 碍 describes something solid, like a stone, blocking one's path.
㝵 gives a sound closely related to ài, though pronunciation has drifted somewhat over time.

example.hanzi: 语言不通阻碍了双方的交流。
example.pinyin: Yǔyán bùtōng zǔ'ài le shuāngfāng de jiāoliú.
example.english: The language barrier hindered communication between the two sides.
example.fact: The Great Barrier Reef off the coast of Australia stretches over 1,400 miles and is large enough to be seen from space, yet rising ocean temperatures have caused repeated mass coral bleaching events since 2016, obstructing the reef's ability to recover between heat waves.

meanings: (of a system or device) to start operating automatically

components.note: 廾 (two hands) — depicts hands at work.
一 represents the latch or bar of a door; hands lifting it away gave 开 its meaning 'to open, to start.'
户 (a door) — the panel of a door.
口 (an opening) — the door swinging open, together giving 启 its meaning 'to open, to begin.'

example.hanzi: 这项发明开启了人类通信的新时代。
example.pinyin: Zhè xiàng fāmíng kāiqǐ le rénlèi tōngxìn de xīn shídài.
example.english: This invention opened up a new era of human communication.
example.fact: Samuel Morse's first public long-distance telegraph message, sent in 1844 between Washington, D.C. and Baltimore, read 'What hath God wrought' — a message that took mere seconds to transmit over 38 miles of wire and helped open the era of near-instant long-distance communication.

components.note: 禾 (grain) ties 称 to its original meaning of weighing grain on a scale.
尔 (ěr) is close in sound to 称's reading chēng; weighing grain to determine its worth extended over time to the senses 'to weigh,' 'to claim,' and 'to be called.'
亻 (person) plus 乍 (suddenly/for the first time) — together suggesting a person making or doing something for the first time.

example.hanzi: 这种现象在物理学中被称作量子纠缠。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng xiànxiàng zài wùlǐxué zhōng bèi chēngzuò liàngzǐ jiūchán.
example.english: This phenomenon is called quantum entanglement in physics.
example.fact: Albert Einstein famously dismissed quantum entanglement as 'spooky action at a distance,' skeptical that particles could instantaneously affect one another across vast distances. Decades later, experiments confirmed entanglement is real, and the physicists who demonstrated it won the 2022 Nobel Prize in Physics.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — 宪 relates to an overarching structure of rules, as in a nation's 'constitution.'
先 (xiān) gives a sound very close to xiàn, sharing the initial and rhyme — only the tone differs.
氵 (water/stream) — water naturally follows a fixed course, an image linked to the idea of 'law' or 'method.'
去 (to go/a course) — the path a stream follows suggested a regulated, consistent way of doing things, hence 'law, method.'

example.hanzi: 美国宪法于1787年制定。
example.pinyin: Měiguó xiànfǎ yú 1787 nián zhìdìng.
example.english: The US Constitution was drafted in 1787.
example.fact: The Constitution of San Marino, a tiny microstate inside Italy, is considered by some historians to be the oldest still-functioning written constitution in the world, with roots tracing back to statutes written in 1600, predating the US Constitution by nearly two centuries.

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — 道 relates to a path or road one walks along.
首 (shǒu) is the historical phonetic element; its modern reading no longer resembles dào, a reminder that sound components can drift after thousands of years of pronunciation change.
八 (two hands) — holding something up.
目 (a container/tray) — held between the two hands, the image behind 具's meaning 'tool, utensil.'

example.hanzi: 演员在舞台上使用了很多道具。
example.pinyin: Yǎnyuán zài wǔtái shàng shǐyòng le hěn duō dàojù.
example.english: The actors used many props on stage.
example.fact: The lightsabers used throughout the original Star Wars trilogy were built around the flash handles of 1970s-era Graflex camera flash units, a prop-department improvisation that has since become one of the most recognizable pieces of movie weaponry in film history.

components.note: Foot/leg shape — represents walking.
Suggests scattered, uncultivated land, giving a sense of something sparse.
散 traditionally depicts a hand (攵) scattering something, like seeds tossed from a basket — the image behind its meaning 'to scatter, disperse.'

example.hanzi: 台风来临前,居民被紧急疏散到安全地带。
example.pinyin: Táifēng láilín qián, jūmín bèi jǐnjí shūsàn dào ānquán dìdài.
example.english: Before the typhoon arrived, residents were urgently evacuated to safe areas.
example.fact: Ahead of Hurricane Rita in 2005, roughly 2.5 million people evacuated the Houston area over a few days, creating gridlock so severe that some drivers spent more than 24 hours covering under 100 miles — a scale of movement that later reshaped how Gulf Coast cities plan hurricane evacuations.

components.note: 走 (to walk/run) — 超 relates to overtaking or surpassing someone while moving
召 (zhào) gives a sound distantly related to 超's reading chāo, having drifted apart over time
屮 (a young sprout) growing up and out of 凵 (a container or pit) — a picture of something emerging, hence 'going out.'

example.hanzi: 这次旅行的花费超出了我们的预算。
example.pinyin: Zhè cì lǚxíng de huāfèi chāochū le wǒmen de yùsuàn.
example.english: The cost of this trip exceeded our budget.
example.fact: The Sydney Opera House was originally budgeted at about 7 million Australian dollars in 1957 but ended up costing roughly 102 million dollars by its 1973 completion — a cost overrun of more than 1,300% that remains one of the most famous in architectural history.

components.note: 幺 (small, little) on the left conveys smallness.
力 (strength) on the right shows limited strength, giving 幼 its meaning 'young, immature.'
禾 (grain) — 稚 originally described a late-ripening grain, extending to mean 'young, immature.'
隹 (zhuī) gives a sound distantly related to zhì, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 他觉得那种想法太幼稚了。
example.pinyin: Tā juéde nà zhǒng xiǎngfǎ tài yòuzhì le.
example.english: He felt that kind of thinking was too childish.
example.fact: Baby elephants suck their trunks the way human infants suck their thumbs, a self-soothing behavior researchers have observed particularly when a calf is stressed, hungry, or separated from its mother, showing that even large, intelligent animals retain distinctly juvenile comfort habits.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh/body) — 背 refers to the back, a part of the body
北 (běi) gives a sound close to 背's reading bèi, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
勹 (an enclosing shape) — wrapping around.
巳 (a baby) — swaddled inside, the image of wrapping something up giving 包 its meaning 'to wrap; bag, package.'

example.hanzi: 他背着一个大背包去旅行。
example.pinyin: Tā bēi zhe yī gè dà bēibāo qù lǔxíng.
example.english: He traveled carrying a large backpack.
example.fact: Ötzi the Iceman, a naturally mummified body from around 3,300 BC found frozen in the Alps in 1991, was discovered carrying a wood-framed backpack made of hazel and larch branches — making it one of the oldest known examples of a human carrying gear in a pack.

components.note: 止 (stop, foot) — a fork in the road is about a path one walks.
支 (zhī) gives a sound distantly related to qí, having drifted apart over time.
见 (to see) — relates directly to 视's meaning 'to look at, view.'
礻 (a form of 示, shì) gives the sound — 视 is also pronounced shì, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 这部法律旨在消除职场中的性别歧视。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù fǎlǜ zhǐzài xiāochú zhíchǎng zhōng de xìngbié qíshì.
example.english: This law aims to eliminate gender discrimination in the workplace.
example.fact: The US Civil Rights Act of 1964 outlawed employment discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, or national origin; the inclusion of 'sex' was reportedly added late in the legislative process by an opponent hoping to sink the bill, yet the act passed and became a landmark of American law.

components.note: 木 (wood) — 极 originally named the ridgepole, the highest beam of a roof, extended to 'extreme, utmost.'
及 (jí) gives the sound — 极 is also pronounced jí, an exact match.
阝 (a mound/place) — 限 relates to a boundary or limit on a place
艮 (gèn) gives a loose sound connection to 限's reading xiàn

example.hanzi: 登山者挑战了人类体能的极限。
example.pinyin: Dēngshānzhě tiǎozhàn le rénlèi tǐnéng de jíxiàn.
example.english: The climber challenged the limits of human physical endurance.
example.fact: At the summit of Mount Everest, roughly 29,032 feet above sea level, air pressure is only about a third of that at sea level, meaning each breath delivers roughly a third of the oxygen — a physiological extreme so severe that the zone above 26,000 feet is nicknamed the 'death zone.'

components.note: 手 (hand) — in the traditional form 擊, 手 contributed the meaning of striking with force, the source of 击's meaning 'to hit, strike.'
王 (a variant of 玉, meaning jade) — 球 originally referred to a round piece of jade, extended to mean 'ball, sphere'
求 (qiú) gives the sound — 球 is also pronounced qiú, an exact match

example.hanzi: 他一棒击球,把球打出了场外。
example.pinyin: Tā yī bàng jīqiú, bǎ qiú dǎ chū le chǎngwài.
example.english: He hit the ball with one swing, knocking it out of the park.
example.fact: A Major League Baseball pitch can leave a bat and travel back toward the pitcher's mound at over 100 miles per hour, giving the pitcher roughly four-tenths of a second to react — less time than it takes to blink twice — which is why comebacker line drives are considered uniquely dangerous.
